userPosition: Strict gun control reduces gun violence
counterPosition: Gun control laws don't effectively reduce gun violence and may increase vulnerability
content: Kleck and Gertz (1995) used a national survey to estimate how often Americans use guns in self-defense. Their estimates are far higher than those from other surveys, and the figure remains disputed. This record does not rely on any other quantitative claim.

citations.author: Gary Kleck, Marc Gertz
citations.title: Armed Resistance to Crime: The Prevalence and Nature of Self-Defense with a Gun
citations.publication: Journal of Criminal Law and Criminology

limitations: The earlier cross-country, felon-survey and RAND claims were removed: they could not be traced to published sources, and the RAND report (2018) reports inconclusive evidence for most policies but moderate evidence that background checks reduce firearm homicides, which this record had not represented.
Defensive gun use estimates vary widely (60k-2.5M)
Cultural and socioeconomic factors differ across countries
Black market data is inherently incomplete
Study focuses on homicides, not mass shootings specifically
